- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-90+ values), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to correct.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — forecasts remain too high for 3–5 days after a decline.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to overcorrect downward after strong upward moves, then fail to recover.
- In the last 5–10 days of the forecast, model tends to be overly conservative, underestimating upward momentum.
- When history includes a recent high, model often fails to recognize the high as a peak and continues to forecast downward.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the last 5–10 days of history are stable or trending upward — model underperforms during volatile or downward trends.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent history (last 5 days) is underutilized in forecasting, leading to lagged responses.
